🧭 Morning Boost | Job Seekers · Thursday

Ask one person in your network for a genuine introduction to someone else.

A warm introduction from someone who already trusts you carries more weight than any cold message ever will.
Ask directly who they'd recommend you meet, be specific about the kind of person or role, or offer to make an introduction back.
Today I will ask one trusted contact for one specific introduction.
Affirmation: "Asking for help is part of building a real network, not a weakness."

🎯 A moment from this week:

I regularly see candidates handle the pay conversation one of two ways.

Some avoid it entirely. Others lead with a number that undersells them.

Either way, the conversation goes better for the employer than it does for them. Being agreeable doesn't change that. Being prepared does.

The takeaway: research the going range for your role and region before the conversation happens, and know your number before anyone asks for it.

Job seekers: if a recruiter asked for your number tomorrow, would you have one ready?

#SalaryNegotiation #JobSearch #NeoHRUS

Can I show my value clearly, confidently, and in under 90 seconds?

Most interview struggles aren't about qualifications. They're about rambling through an unstructured story. Ascent turns preparation into presence: tight, rehearsed stories and sharp questions that make the interview a two-way conversation about fit, not an interrogation.

Your goal for this phase: Deliver three STAR stories under 90 seconds each and walk into every interview with five company-specific questions of your own.

Could you tell that story again, in half the time?

Watch out for: Rambling, unstructured answers, and showing up with no questions for the interviewer. Both read as under-preparation, not personality.

You're ready to move on when: You can deliver three STAR stories crisply under 90 seconds, with five researched questions ready per company.

🌱 Morning Boost | Job Seekers · Sunday

Grow your network by exactly one person today, someone new, not someone you already talk to.

It's easy to keep reaching out to the same small circle instead of genuinely expanding it.
Follow someone new in your field, comment thoughtfully on their post, or send a short introduction message.
Today I will connect with one new person outside my current circle.
Affirmation: "My network grows one honest connection at a time."

👋 Midday Check-In | Job Seekers · Sunday

Follow up with someone you connected with earlier this week.

A first message without a follow-up often gets forgotten within days on both sides.
Send a short check-in, share something relevant you saw, or ask a specific question to keep it going.
I will follow up with one person I connected with earlier this week.
Affirmation: "A relationship needs more than one message to become real."
